question: A fasciotomy is indicated in compartment syndrome when the compartment pressure exceeds 30 mmHg regardless of the patient's diastolic blood pressure.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is false. The recommended threshold is ΔP < 30 mmHg (diastolic BP minus compartment pressure). An absolute compartment pressure of 30 mmHg can be safe in a normotensive patient (diastolic 80 → ΔP = 50) but dangerous in a hypotensive patient (diastolic 40 → ΔP = 10). Always use ΔP, not absolute pressure alone.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. The operative threshold is ΔP (delta pressure) = diastolic BP minus compartment pressure < 30 mmHg (not an absolute pressure of 30 mmHg). In a hypotensive patient (e.g. diastolic 50 mmHg), even a compartment pressure of 25 mmHg represents ΔP = 25, which is critical. Absolute 30 mmHg is a guide, not the criterion.
